steps.domain_action: The target molecule strychnine is defined as the initial object of analysis

The molecule is disconnected into the indole and piperidine precursors

Alternative disconnections leading to unstable radicals are rejected
The conceptual fragments are reunited to validate the retrosynthetic logic
The retrosynthetic plan is recorded as the formal synthetic strategy
Forward synthesis commences with the condensation of phenylhydrazine and acetophenone
The Fischer indole synthesis produces the initial bicyclic core
Introduction of the veratryl group via alkylation
Formation of the tricyclic intermediate through ring closure
Verification of the regioselectivity of the aromatic substitution
Isolation and purification of the crystalline intermediate
The route branches into parallel functional group manipulations
Successful reduction of the nitro group to the amine
Attempted direct cyclization fails due to steric hindrance
Re-evaluation of the protecting group strategy
Recombination of the modified fragments into the tetracyclic precursor
Dieckmann condensation forms the fifth ring
The intermediate exists as a mixture of enol and keto tautomers
Selenium dioxide oxidation introduces the necessary unsaturation
Final skeletal rearrangements to form the isostrychnine framework
Comparison of synthetic isostrychnine with the degradation product
Base-catalyzed isomerization of isostrychnine to strychnine
The final product matches the natural alkaloid properties
The total synthesis is finalized and published in the permanent record
The synthetic cycle is closed and the system boundary is reached
